```data
orchestrator/skill_router.py:10 MANDATORY maps role "review"/"spec_review" to skill id "reviewer/adversarial-review" and "challenge" to "reviewer/challenge", but the actual registry ids (skill_id = f"{role}/{directory_name}" from skills_registry.sync(), directories skills/review/adversarial-review and skills/review/challenge) are "review/adversarial-review" and "review/challenge" — there is no "reviewer/*" skill. Verified by running skills_registry.sync() against the real skills/ tree: it emits 'review/adversarial-review': roles ['review','spec_review'] and 'review/challenge': roles ['challenge']. For every review, spec_review, and challenge spawn in shadow mode, selected will contain a phantom id that is never actually exposed or used, so (a) token accounting silently zeroes out for that mandatory skill (records.get(id, {}) misses), and (b) the real used id (review/adversarial-review or review/challenge) will never match anything in skills_selected, so decision_log.outcome's skill_recovery diff fires on essentially every review/spec_review/challenge run — corrupting exactly the P30 skill_recovery_rate metric this task exists to produce for 3 of the ~6 routed roles. If Stage 5 later makes 'active' gate real exposure, reviewers/challengers would lose their mandatory skill entirely. The unit tests don't catch this because they use synthetic registries with ids that happen to match the (wrong) MANDATORY strings instead of syncing the real skills/ directory.
```
